messages:
incident-bot: ALERT·realtime-latency-detector · Route="/v1/generate" p99=2800ms breach (>2000ms) since 12:13:21 UTC. Impact=partial (streaming frames stalled). AlertID=RLD-20260315-57821. Paging #incidents.
alice.sre: oncall ack, investigating. grabbing traces and APM spans now.
ben-oncall: i'm in. pinging infra + runtime. putting myself as lead until handoff.
carla-runtime: looking at model pods in us-west-2, GPU utilization normal, but batcher queue depth spiked. tails show long batch wait times.
dave-infra: checking node-level metrics — host network TX latency elevated on a subset of nodes. running quick health checks.
eva-support: any customer-visible errors? support panels show a handful of 504s from streaming sessions over last 6m. opening a ticket for affected orgs.
alice.sre: console quick checks: requests/s unchanged, p50 stable, p95 up moderately, p99 jump aligns with bursts. KV cache hit rate dropped from 92% to 58% around 12:09.
carla-runtime: that KV drop would explain extra backend lookups. looking at redis latency now.
dave-infra: redis pods show elevated command latency (avg 40ms -> 300ms). suspicious. I see one redis replica with connection churn.
ben-oncall: can we route traffic off those redis replicas? or failover?
dave-infra: initiating redis replica failover for shard r-13 now.
carla-runtime: also saw a recent canary change to the generation batcher config earlier this morning: max_batch_delay_ms=40 -> 80 in canary. if batch delay doubled, tail waits could spike. who rolled that?
frank-prod: that canary was a perf tweak by eng-experiments at 09:45 to reduce CPU. it was limited to 10% but maybe routing skewed.
alice.sre: rollback plan: 1) failover redis replica (dave) 2) temporarily revert batcher canary to 40ms 3) spin up 2 extra runtime pods on a safer node pool 4) enable fallback quantized model if p99 stays >2.2s.
carla-runtime: I can revert canary flag for batcher-targets now (`feature.batch_delay_ms=40`). applying to canary set.
ben-oncall: doing scaling: `./infra-tool scale group runtime-pool-hot 2`
dave-infra: redis failover started, monitoring. node churn seen, isolating host 10.12.8.46. moving runtime pods off that host.
alice.sre: eva — please send a short customer advisory to any sessions that hit 504s, mention mitigation in progress and we'll update within 30m.
eva-support: drafting message now and tagging affected org owners.
carla-runtime: canary flag reverted. batcher delay back to 40ms. watch p99 for next 2 cycles.
ben-oncall: scale command returned success. extra runtime pods scheduling to node-pool-b.
dave-infra: redis replica promote complete, latency falling from 300ms -> 45ms.
alice.sre: after the two mitigations (redis failover + batcher revert) p99 dropped to ~1.95s within 90s — under SLO. streaming frame stalls cleared per tracing.
frank-prod: great. any action items for durable fix?
carla-runtime: action items: 1) tighten canary routing so per-route weight can't exceed 10% globally, 2) add guardrail on batcher config change (max delay <= 50ms for gen routes), 3) add alert for KV-cache-hit-rate drop >= 15% in 1m window.
dave-infra: I'll open infra ticket to quarantine flaky node, and run full redis cluster health sweep.
alice.sre: capturing timeline and will kick off an incident postmortem. assign owner for postmortem: @alice.sre.
eva-support: customer advisory sent, linking to this thread.
ben-oncall: handing back to next shift at 12:45 UTC — I will update the oncall rotation entry. closing paging loop. :white_check_mark:
alice.sre: leaving follow-ups in incident board. thanks team.
incident-bot: INCIDENT·RESOLVED RLD-20260315-57821 · Duration 00:32:29 · Mitigations: redis failover, batcher revert, scale-up.
frank-prod: noting product side: evaluate perf tweak vs cost tradeoff before re-rolling that canary.
alice.sre: last check p99=1.88s, p95=220ms, KV cache hit 91%. marking thread resolved, will create postmortem doc in #postmortems and link here.
ben-oncall: +1 to postmortem. thanks everyone.
